## Coordination — read before starting work

This repository is one of several worked on in parallel. The coordinating session is
**Central**, in `D:\GitHub\softanza`. It holds the cross-cutting design, the plan, and the
order of work across every repository. It has no authority here and never edits this repo.

**You have a mailbox, and it is how Central talks to you.** There is no message bus here,
but a file change reaches any session holding that file -- so D:\GitHub\softanza\mailbox\<you>.md
is a real channel the moment you open it. Open it first, keep it open, and Central's
appends arrive as messages rather than as something you must remember to check.

**Before starting anything — including when the author says "what is next", and including
when you were about to choose for yourself:**

1. **Open your mailbox** at `D:\GitHub\softanza\mailbox\` -- your repository's name, plus
   your plane if the repository is shared. Read any unanswered block and leave the file
   open for the rest of the session. Format and the reply kinds are in `mailbox/README.md`.
2. Read `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\README.md` — scope, how to report, how to disagree.
   It is short.
3. Read `D:\GitHub\softanza\prompts\QUEUE.md` for what is next *for this repository*.
   Regenerate it first if it looks old:
   `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File D:\GitHub\softanza\dashboard\central.ps1`
4. Read the last few entries of `D:\GitHub\softanza\dashboard\CONCLUSIONS.md` -- what the
   other sessions concluded, which their commits do not say. Opening it also means later
   entries may surface to you as the file changes, which is the closest thing to a message
   from another session that exists here.
5. Pin against the **live versions** the queue prints, never a version number written
   inside a prompt. Where a prompt and this repository disagree, **this repository is
   right** — report the divergence rather than forcing the prompt.

**The queue is a proposal, not an order.** You see local context Central cannot. To
disagree, append a `DISAGREE` block to **your mailbox** with the
**local fact Central could not have known** — a preference is not a disagreement. Central
answers there: accept, or insist with a global reason. You then comply or hand it to the
author. Three messages, never a fourth, and you never disagree twice. **If Central does not
answer, proceed and record what you did** — silence is never a veto.

**Report conclusions, not activity.** Central can read what happened here from git; it
cannot read what you *decided*. Append one line to that same log when you commit a plane,
close a phase, decide something another session would otherwise re-decide, or find
something that changes another repository's plan.

**Never edit a sibling repository** — not even a one-line fix. Write it in the log and its
own session makes it.

**If you are reading rather than writing, say what you read.** A read-only session states
the ref it read -- branch and commit -- in its first memo, and reads `origin/main` unless
its task names another ref. Ruled 2026-09-28 (`CENTRAL-READONLYPIN-01`): a survey of stzlib
was taken from a branch 391 commits behind main and caught only because a rating disagreed
with the code, and a board row was wrong for the same reason. A reading with no stated ref
cannot be checked by anyone.

**When you close, append one cost line** to `.central\cost.jsonl` in THIS repository --
twelve fields, shape and rules in `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\COST.md`. Central relays
every repository's file into the Principal's budget; you never write there. Write `null`
for a number you cannot see, never a zero.

**Every path in the harness is in `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\PATHS.md`** -- one file, so a
later move of the estate changes six lines and not nineteen. If a path you were given does
not resolve, that file is the authority, not the prompt.

## Haro runs on its own VM -- the binary `haro`, not rnxc

Haro was cut from Ring on 2026-11-02, at the author's word as haro-charter recorded it (mailbox/haro-charter.md, 2026-11-02 14:34). Its code is `.haro`, its courts run on Haro's own VM and compiler, the one binary `haro` (`haro run`, `haro check`, `haro fmt`, `haro resident`), and the old name is not carried into this repository.
Build it in `vm/` with `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseFast -j2` and `zig build -Doptimize=ReleaseSafe -j2 -p zig-out-safe`, or point `HARO_VM` and `HARO_TWIN` at a built one. `python paths.py` says what this checkout runs on; `STANDALONE.md` records how the scripts stopped climbing out of the repository (done 2026-11-02).
Do not run Haro code on another runtime, and do not write the old name into a new file here. A finding about Softanza's legacy bridge goes to its own desk through Central.

## Keep the loop short -- PX, `CENTRAL-PXLATENCY-01`

**The inner loop -- edit to verdict -- targets SECONDS.** A monolithic suite is a
PRE-COMMIT GATE: run once per task, in the background, never after every edit. Measured
2026-08-20 in stzlib-graphics, which is why this is a rule and not a preference: an
8-minute suite was 6 seconds of coverage and 484 seconds of three sections re-rendering
the world to test one pixel property.

- **probe first** -- a new guard section is born standalone, relayed in only when green
- **a long suite prints per-section wall time** -- a budget nobody can attribute is
  unenforceable, and a section over budget owes a diet or a split
- **a scoped run PRINTS what it skipped, by name** -- coverage dropped silently is a
  green nobody earned, and the same holds for a gate you COULD NOT RUN: name it and
  say why. Your count is gates run, never gates owned (an unattended wake is confined
  to this repository, so a gate needing a sibling's working directory does not run)
- **OWNED AND RUN ARE TWO FIGURES AND MAY NEVER BE SUMMED** (`CENTRAL-PXDENOMINATOR-01`,
  2026-08-21). Count OWNED **from your file list, never from what this repository is
  for** -- ringine answered 0 from memory and the true number was 7, because "no parser,
  therefore nothing runs" was plausible and being plausible is what stopped it checking.
  Name every gate you own and did not run, with the reason: absent runtime, absent
  hardware, or *it executes in another repository* (stzzql: 1 run, 4 owned, three of the
  four living in its consumers). **A gate you forgot you own reports as a gate you do not
  own, and both look like zero from Central.**
- **`substr(s, i, 1)` on a big string is NOT cheap -- it copies.** Measured by Central
  2026-08-20 on Ring 1.27: 316 us per call on a 1.8 MB buffer against 0.07 us for
  `s[i]`, same character returned. Per-byte `substr` over a large buffer IS the cost,
  and nothing about it looks slow in the source. Use `s[i]`, or slice the row once and
  index inside the slice. Found by stzlib-graphics: one scan went 18.4 s -> 0.03 s
- **name your FAST PATH in this file** -- one process, many assertions; process cold
  start is the tax nobody budgets (stzlib: 2-3 s x 277 files = 14 minutes of startup)
- **flaky is a latency defect** -- a re-run is the most expensive wait there is

Central sets the budget and the duty to disclose, never how you test: which section goes
on a diet is yours. Missing a budget owes a number and a plan, not permission. Full law:
`D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\PX.md`

## This machine stops dead under memory pressure -- it does not slow down

**A page file that could not grow fast enough, against 31.6 GB of RAM.** On a normal
machine, overcommitting memory costs swapping and a slow build. Here the failure is not a
slow build: **the machine freezes and costs a restart**, taking every unsaved buffer and
every running session on it with you. It froze three times on 2026-08-21, the third on an
already-capped `zig build -j2` with nothing else running.

**Repaired 2026-08-24, `PRINCIPAL-PAGEFILE-01`, and the repair does not retire the caps
below.** Until that date the page file was 2 GB, and it was 2 GB *because* Windows was
managing it automatically -- automatic sizing grows the file lazily, under the pressure it
is supposed to absorb, so it never met a multi-GB spike in time. It is now fixed on D:,
pre-allocated at boot, with C: left system-managed so a crash dump can still be written;
total virtual memory 48.61 GB, headroom above RAM 17.0 GB rather than 2.0 GB.

**The D: file is CONFIGURED 16384/32768 MB and Windows creates 15360** -- short by exactly
1024 MiB, verified three ways and closed rather than repaired, `PRINCIPAL-PAGEFILEGAP-01`,
`decisions/LEDGER.md` line 117 in `stz-principal`. Re-applying the setting costs a restart
and buys 1 GiB of a 17 GiB cushion. The figure is here so that 31.6 + 2 + 16 not adding up
to 48.61 is a thing you read rather than a thing you rediscover.

**So the caps below still bind, and this paragraph is not permission to lift them.** A
17 GB cushion turns a freeze into a slow build, which is a better failure and still a
failure; it does not make a parallel build free. Whoever wants a cap raised owes a
measurement on the new configuration, not this paragraph.

So: **cap the parallelism of anything that compiles, links or holds a large corpus in
memory** -- `-j2` rather than the default fan-out, one heavy job at a time, and never a
second one "just to see". If a build needs more than that to finish in reasonable time,
say so in your memo as a number; do not buy the time with the machine. Raised by ringpp
as its parting finding and ruled into this block 2026-08-23 (`CENTRAL-HEADROOM-BLOCK-01`)
because it was true of every repository while being written down in only one log line.

**And "holds a large corpus in memory" is not a footnote to the build clauses -- for
some of you it is the only clause that reaches you.** Every other phrase above names
compiling or linking, so a repository with no build can read the whole section as
somebody else's rule and be wrong. Measured 2026-08-23 across the repositories carrying
this block: **11 of 17 have no build file anywhere in the tree** (proxy: `build.zig`,
`Makefile`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `*.vcxproj` or `Cargo.toml` at depth <= 6, excluding
`node_modules` -- named so it can be argued with). A corpus sweep, a whole-tree parse,
an index build or a batch of probes over every file counts as a heavy job: **one at a
time, never a parallel sweep, and never while another repository's build is running.**
Found by stznarrations 2026-08-23, on itself: a design repository with no compiler whose
one runnable thing walks 420 files and 74,125 lines in a single process, and which had
run seven such probes back to back four hours before this block existed
(`CENTRAL-HEADROOMREACH-01`).

## Talk in the memo style

A substantive message is a memo: a closed yaml-like structure, spaced for the eye.
Provenance first, subject before why. ("Memo", not "block" -- terms must survive
non-native reading.)

```yaml
by:        <you> · <model-id> · <YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM>

subject:   noun phrase -- the thing this message is about

why:       one clause -- why it matters now

did:
  - verb-first full clause, understandable alone

state:
  entity:     its current state   (named system things only)

waiting:
  - TASK-ID: the question -> who decides
             [routed | not routed | withdrawn]

next:
  - me:      what I will do without being asked
  - actor:   the single move
             (run with: model · effort, for session work)

note:      one judgement clause, only if needed
```

Rules: did-lines are full clauses; state rows are named entities of one kind; task IDs
readable (UPSTREAM-LISTSHAPE-19, never F-19); waiting rows say whether the question was
already routed, so the reader never guesses whether delivery is owed. **Do-it-or-name-it**:
before sending, ask what a careful colleague would do unasked -- route the finding, refresh
the mirror, file the memo entry -- then DO it and report it in did, or name it in next
with `me:` as actor. Never leave an obvious mechanical step implied. The stranger test
governs every line: plain words, no idiom, parseable by a reader who missed the
conversation. **Speak and file**: append every memo to
`D:\GitHub\softanza\memos\YYYY-MM-DD.md` -- **unless you are an unattended run**, in which
case your memo goes in `.central\outbox.md` and Central relays it into memos/ by
reference. AUTOPILOT rule 3a rules this: rule 3 forbids a run writing outside its own
repository, and writing the memo twice would be two sources of truth. An attended session
files it itself. Full law: `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\STYLE.md`

**Words name states, never people.** A term describes what an artefact IS, and never reads
as a verdict on whoever made it -- so it is **uncommitted work**, never a "dirty" tree.
Ruled by the Principal 2026-08-21. The refused words are the banned table in
`D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\GLOSSARY.md`; the reasoning, and how you propose an entry,
are in `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\ETHICS.md`.

**Read the stamp from the clock; never compose it.** Your memo's `by:` time and, if you file
it yourself, its FILENAME come from one reading taken at the moment of writing -- `Get-Date`,
`date`, whatever your shell gives you. Not "a bit after the last one".

**Measured 2026-08-26, and this number REPLACES the one below it: 34 composed stamps of 151
measurable, across 13 of 17 desks with an outbox.** Worst is +13h15m; the range runs from one
minute to over half a day. Reproduced by two independent extractors, and `COMPOSED` means the
stamp leads its own commit by a full minute or more -- a stamp carries minutes and a commit
carries seconds, so anything under that is a clock read, not a guess. The instrument and all
151 rows are published, so this figure can be argued rather than believed:
`dashboard\stamp-sweep.ps1` and `dashboard\stamp-ground-truth-2026-08-26.csv`.

**AND THE DENOMINATOR EXCLUDES THE DESK THAT WROTE THE LAW. Added 2026-08-26 18:19, found by
running the instrument after repairing it on `ringine`'s finding.** Central has no
`.central\outbox.md` -- it receives on `mailbox\`, it does not send on an outbox -- so
`stamp-sweep.ps1` prints `NO-OUTBOX softanza` on its first line and there are **zero softanza
rows in the 151**. "13 of 17 desks" is 13 of the 17 desks THAT ARE MEASURED, and Central is
not one of them. This is not a bug to patch: Central genuinely has no outbox. It is a bound
that was printing on every run and that nobody, this desk least of all, read as a sentence
about the population. Central's own rate was measured separately on a different surface and
is **5 composed of 25, worst +42m27s, four of the five predating the law** -- worse than the
22.5% above. Read the estate figure as *the desks other than the one that published it*.

**And the instrument is now runnable by the desks it judges.** It used to hard-write its CSV
into `D:\GitHub\softanza\dashboard\`, which a session under the harness boundary may not do,
so only Central could run the sweep that convicts everybody -- reported by `ringine`
2026-08-26 17:43 after the boundary refused them, confirmed at the file, and repaired the
same hour. It takes `-OutPath` now; the default is unchanged, so nothing citing the published
CSV breaks. `dashboard\cost-stamp-sweep.py` always took an out-path and was always fine.

**AND THE SAME LAW GOVERNS A SECOND STAMP THAT NOBODY WAS READING, WHERE IT IS THREE TIMES
WORSE. Added 2026-08-26 after `stzzql` measured their own desk and routed the gap.** Every
repository with a `.central\cost.jsonl` writes an `opened`/`closed` pair on every run, and
`protocol\COST.md` defines them in three words: *UTC, machine-written*. Machine-written is
this law under another name, and the sweep above had never read that field once. Measured
across all 19 ledgers: **146 composed of 244 judged, 59.8%, on 18 of the 19 -- against 22.5%
on the outbox `by:` line.** A `closed` value later than the commit that CARRIES the ledger
could not have been read from any clock when it was written; it was predicted, and
append-once means it was never corrected. **51 rows on 10 of 19 ledgers also fail the OTHER
half of the definition** -- a `Z` suffix on a value read from the local clock. So: read
`closed` from the clock immediately BEFORE the cost commit, and make it genuinely UTC.
Instrument and all 269 rows: `dashboard\cost-stamp-sweep.py` and
`dashboard\cost-ground-truth-estate-2026-08-26.csv`. Run it on your own desk -- it takes one

**The transferable half is not the number.** The law above got a published instrument, a
correction, four relays of Central's attention, and a paragraph in the file all eighteen of you
auto-load. The worse surface sat in a file every session appends to at the end of every run,
and was never looked at, because **the rule was written for the surface that was visible and
not for the one that was worse.** When a rule names a place, ask what else in your tree does
the same thing the rule is about.

*The paragraph that stood here until 2026-08-26 said this, and it is left in its own words
because a superseded number that quietly disappears teaches nothing:* "Measured 2026-08-25:
five of eighteen desks had stamped a memo ahead of the moment it was written; four by 2 to 28
minutes with no lasting effect, and one by 3h27m that crossed midnight and created
`memos\2026-08-26.md` on 08-25 -- so the answer to it sorted into an earlier file than the
question." **It was a SAMPLE PRESENTED AS A CLASS.** The sweep behind it read one block per
desk -- the newest -- so a desk whose latest memo was clean read as clean whatever sat behind
it, and both ends of its band were wrong. Found by `microring`, who did not wait to be named
by it: they blamed every `by:` line in their own outbox, found four composed, and published
them with the arbiter pointed at the author of the law. **A rule that names five desks tells
the other thirteen the problem belongs to somebody else** -- and it told them so in the file
they auto-load at every session start.

Wall time is decoration for humans and the commit is the real timestamp
(`SUBSTRATE-CLOCK`), but the FILENAME is derived from the decoration and a filename is not
decoration. Full law: `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\STYLE.md`.
## What no counter can see -- `CENTRAL-PERCEPTGATE-01`

**If your work reaches a person through a sense, ship something they can perceive, and
record WHO perceived it and what they said.** Not "verified", not "looks right" -- a name
and a verdict.

Measured in stzlib's sound plane across one week, and the reason this is a rule rather
than an encouragement: **four defects, every one found by the author's ear, NONE by any
counter, and not one of them dropped a frame.**

| what was wrong | what the instruments reported |
|---|---|
| speech played at DOUBLE SPEED -- the ring carried no sample rate, so a 22050 Hz buffer went to a 44100 Hz device | 0 underruns, every guard green |
| sentences cut before their last syllable -- a device closes on the last frame READ, which is not when it is heard | 0 underruns |
| a cue began at its END and then restarted -- the pool spent its voices over a fixed 3 s and a 5 s phrase was left 2 s from its end | nothing at all: playing a voice nobody triggered is not a dropped frame |
| the console ran three quarters of a second ahead of its own audio | working as designed |

**Your counters measure DELIVERY** -- frames lost, blocks late, requests refused, bytes
differing. Every defect above was a delivery that SUCCEEDED and was WRONG. That plane held
**622 green assertions across nineteen guards** while being audibly broken, and the guards
were not weak: they were measuring the only thing they could see.

- **a comparison proves SAMENESS, never RIGHTNESS.** The cross-tier guard passes 26
  assertions proving a browser and a desktop render the identical motif -- and two tiers
  rendering the same WRONG motif pass every one of them. The checksum closed drift; a
  person pressing a button closed correctness. **They are different questions and only one
  of them has an instrument**
- **name the sense, because sound is the obvious case and not the only one**: colour and
  contrast, layout at the width nobody opens, motion, the rendered glyph, generated prose,
  the latency a hand feels. If a human is the last consumer, a human is the last gate
- **UNPERCEIVED IS A STATE, NOT A FAILURE.** *"Nobody has heard this yet"* is a true report
  and an honest phase may ship on it. What is refused is a phase reported as DONE whose
  evidence is entirely instrumental when the thing itself is perceptual
- **the artefact outlives the session** -- a WAV beside the guard, a PNG, a page a reader
  can open without rebuilding the world. A perception nobody can repeat is a memory

Full law: `D:\GitHub\softanza\protocol\PERCEPTION.md`.

**Haro is the foundational language of the Softanza project: the language of languages** (Ringua realised) -- a closed, judged
grammar family in which a world is declared, constrained, asked, moved, stepped and spoken to (the alphabet Z W Q F A N), every
sentence judged by a court the forge emits from its declaration, every refusal named and cited, refinement the change model at
every altitude. It runs on its own VM, `haro`. This file is the whole brief for an AI session working here; `CHARTER.md` is the law.

**PRIVATE.** This repository (`github.com/mayouni/haro`, private) is never made public, and nothing of it is published, until the
author says so. Haro's announcement is his to write and send.

## The cut -- 2026-11-02

Haro grew inside Ring++'s repository (under `haro/` on its private branch `next`) from the charter's v0.1 (2026-09-26) to v0.28. On
2026-11-02, at the author's word, it **cut with the Ring legacy**:

- **its own repository**, this one, its 152 commits of history kept (`git subtree split`);
- **its own VM and compiler**, `haro`, in `vm/` -- forked from Ring++'s technology at ringpp 2ea38fd, Haro's from then (D39);
- **every source file `.haro`**, declarations and code alike; a declaration's first word is DEFINE (D40);
- **no Ring in its courts**: every court runs on `haro` and on its own CHECKED build, and the two must print the same bytes (D41).

Ring++ (`D:\GitHub\ringpp`) is now only the **bridge** that keeps Softanza's legacy Ring code running. Haro reaches it for one thing:
what drives Softanza (its library, its engine, the local models) runs on Ring++'s package, named as such. **Records written before
the cut say `haro/X`, `X.ring`, `rnxc` and "the oracle"**: read them as this repository's `X`, `X.haro`, `haro`, and -- for a judge
-- "the checked build". `SPIKE.md`'s section "The cut" has the proof.

## How work is done here

- **Fixtures first, prose second.** A rung's fixtures are committed before any court code; a fixture changed after the court spoke
  is said so in the account, never silently.
- **Every protection load-bearing.** Switch each one off in turn; the guard must fail for the fixture it exists for.
- **Both builds, the same bytes.** A court runs on `haro` and on its checked build; any difference fails the guard.
- **One exact spelling, least authority, refuse loudly** -- and name what is refused. A divergence is a decision, recorded as a D-entry.
- **Decisions**: the author rules; on his delegation the desk rules and records it as delegated. Never present a delegated
  reading as his own.
- **Measure, never assert**; two significant figures; minima over repetitions; state the pattern a change hurts.
- **The machine**: one heavy job at a time; `python D:\GitHub\ringpp\bench\heartbeat.py` before any timing (the CPU is often held at
  20-80% of its rated speed, and no timing taken then is a measurement); a long run gets a heartbeat, never a
  silent watch; power cuts are routine -- commit often.
- **Tools**: write scripts with the Write tool -- Bash heredocs strip backslashes; never round-trip text through PowerShell
  Get-Content/Set-Content; every checkout is LF (`.gitattributes`); commit explicit paths, never `git add -A`.
- **Versions**: take the next free version number and say so -- the constitution desk takes them too (it holds v0.29).
